In [[mathematics]], a function of '''bounded deformation''' is a function whose [[distributional derivative]]s are not quite [[well-behaved]]-enough to qualify as functions of [[bounded variation]], although the symmetric part of the derivative matrix does meet that condition. Thought of as deformations of [[elasticity (physics)|elasto]]-[[plasticity (physics)|plastic]] bodies, functions of bounded deformation play a major role in the mathematical study of [[materials science|materials]], e.g. the Francfort-Marigo model of [[fracture|brittle crack evolution]].

More precisely, given an [[open set|open subset]] &Omega; of '''R'''<sup>''n''</sup>, a function ''u''&nbsp;:&nbsp;&Omega;&nbsp;&rarr;&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''n''</sup> is said to be of '''bounded deformation''' if the [[symmetrized gradient]] ''&epsilon;''(''u'') of ''u'',

:<math>\varepsilon(u) = \frac{\nabla u + \nabla u^{\top}}{2}</math>

is a [[bounded function|bounded]], [[symmetric matrix|symmetric]] ''n''&nbsp;&times;&nbsp;''n'' matrix-valued [[Radon measure]]. The collection of all functions of bounded deformation is denoted BD(&Omega;;&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''n''</sup>), or simply BD, introduced essentially by P.-M. Suquet in 1978. BD is a strictly larger space than the space BV of functions of [[bounded variation]].

One can show that if ''u'' is of bounded deformation then the measure ''&epsilon;''(''u'') can be decomposed into three parts: one [[absolutely continuous]] with respect to [[Lebesgue measure]], denoted ''e''(''u'')&nbsp;d''x''; a jump part, [[support (measure theory)|supported]] on a rectifiable (''n''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1)-dimensional set ''J''<sub>''u''</sub> of points where ''u'' has two different approximate limits ''u''<sub>+</sub> and ''u''<sub>&minus;</sub>, together with a [[normal vector]] ''&nu;''<sub>''u''</sub>; and a "[[Cantor set|Cantor part]]", which vanishes on Borel sets of finite ''H''<sup>''n''&minus;1</sup>-measure (where ''H''<sup>''k''</sup> denotes ''k''-dimensional [[Hausdorff measure]]).

A function ''u'' is said to be of '''special bounded deformation''' if the Cantor part of ''&epsilon;''(''u'') vanishes, so that the measure can be written as

:<math>\varepsilon(u) = e(u) \, \mathrm{d} x + \big( u_{+}(x) - u_{-}(x) \big) \odot \nu_{u} (x) H^{n - 1} | J_{u},</math>

where ''H''<sup>&nbsp;''n''&minus;1</sup>&nbsp;|&nbsp;''J''<sub>''u''</sub> denotes ''H''<sup>&nbsp;''n''&minus;1</sup> on the jump set ''J''<sub>''u''</sub> and <math>\odot</math> denotes the symmetrized [[dyadic product]]:

:<math>a \odot b = \frac{a \otimes b + b \otimes a}{2}.</math>

The collection of all functions of special bounded deformation is denoted SBD(&Omega;;&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''n''</sup>), or simply SBD.
